newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Yang unsure if knighthood can be surrendered.
newsitem.headline: HK's Yang unsure if knighthood can be surrendered.

text.p: Hong Kong's former chief justice, who quit in September to vie for the top government post in the territory after it reverts to Chinese control, has found it harder to quit his British knighthood.
"I understand through the grape vine that you are not constitutionally able to give up a knighthood. The best you can do is not to use it," Sir Ti Liang Yang told a news conference.
Yang, one of four main contenders for the post-handover job of chief executive, had applied to relinquish his knighthood.

The British colony returns to Chinese control at midnight on June 30, 1997, after which it becomes a Special Administrative Region of China. The chief executive will be selected by a Beijing-appointed body and will likely be announced in December.
